text:
mira: Heads-up: saw duplicated onboarding side-effects from the sample-app during SDK warmup in staging. Two user rows created for one signup flow. Repro steps below.

alex: Ugh, saw something similar last week but assumed it was our webhook retry. Can you paste logs?

mira: Logs: the client SDK does a prewarm probe after token refresh; request-id header is identical for the two calls but the server accepted both and ran side-effects.

mira: Minimal repro (staging): curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/signup -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -H 'X-Request-Id: r-123' -d '{"email":"test+warmup@example.com"}'

sam: Hmm if request-id is identical then server should be deduping. Do we set idempotency keys differently for warmup probes?

mira: SDK prewarm uses same request body + same id header because it replays last request to prime caches. We didn't expect warmup to be treated as a real user action.

jen: Is this sample-app code calling the public signup endpoint or a special warmup endpoint?

mira: Public signup. The sample-app was trying to reduce first-request latency by reissuing the graphql mutation during client init.

deploy-bot: deploy status: staging/api v2.12 deployed 10m ago :white_check_mark:

alex: Proposal: treat warmup probes as "non-final" and mark them with X-Warmup: 1 so backend can skip side-effects (or run in dry-run). That avoids changing idempotency semantics.

sam: I like that. Backend could short-circuit side-effects when X-Warmup=1. Need to be careful about auth checks though.

jen: Alternative: SDK-level safe-replay gate. If SDK is re-sending an in-flight request purely for warmup, it should add an internal header like X-SDK-Warmup and a distinct request-id (or omit idempotency header) so server sees it as a probe.

mira: Both changes preferable. Backend header support is easier for product teams. SDK change required for parity across languages.

alex: SDK impl suggestion (pseudo):
```
# warmup replay logic (pseudocode)
if is_warmup_probe and allow_non_side_effects:
  headers['X-Warmup'] = '1'
  headers['X-Request-Id'] = generate_unique_id()  # so server doesnt treat as real replay
else:
  headers['X-Request-Id'] = caller_provided_id or generate_id()
```

sam: For safe replays (real retries) we still want idempotency keys to dedupe. But warmup should explicitly opt-out. Nice.

mira: One more edge: some customers rely on idempotency for billing dedupe. If warmup uses unique id, they'll be charged for warmup calls. We need billing/stats signals to separate warmup traffic.

alex: Backend telemetry idea: tag requests with warmup=true and emit metrics warmup_count, warmup_latency, warmup_side_effects_filtered. Then billing can ignore warmup tags if desired.

jen: Implementation plan:
- Backend: honor X-Warmup header -> run read-only path, skip side-effects, mark metric (owner @infra).
- SDKs: expose opt-in warmup prefetch flag with default off for now. When enabled, SDK sends X-Warmup and unique idempotency keys.
- Sample-apps: update templates to avoid calling user-affecting endpoints during warmup; use a dedicated warmup endpoint if needed.

mira: Who wants to own the backend change? I'm happy to pair with infra.

sam: I can take SDK JS + go change. Will add feature flag and opt-in config.

alex: I'll update sample-app recipes and docs. Add a note to onboarding guide about avoiding side-effectful warmups.

ops-bot: reminder: add regression test in e2e suite (tag: warmup).

mira: Quick test I ran to validate dedupe: repeated request with same X-Request-Id should be ignored. But our signup mutation had side-effects before dedupe hook kicked in (ordering bug).

sam: Good catch. We should push dedupe earlier in API pipeline (auth -> dedupe -> handlers). I'll file infra ticket.

jen: Could we also add a short safe-replay window config at server-side (default 60s) that treats identical request-ids as duplicates? That helps clients that sometimes replay after brief backoffs.

alex: Proposed defaults: safe_replay_window_sec=60, warmup_header='X-Warmup', warmup_default=false. Documented in SDK config.

mira: Tests to add:
- sample-app with warmup enabled: should not create user rows.
- sample-app without warmup: normal behavior.
- SDK idempotency parity: JS/Python/Go behaviours identical.

sam: I'll prototype JS change this afternoon and share a small patch. Want owners for code review: @mira, @jen.

mira: Thanks — please include a quick curl example in PR showing X-Warmup header.

sam: Will do.

deploy-bot: note: new infra ticket #INF-812 queued (dedupe earlier in pipeline).

alex: TL;DR: warmup should be explicit and non-side-effectful; add header + telemetry + SDK opt-in. Less friction than trying to auto-detect warmup vs real user actions. :+1:

mira: Agreed. Leaving this thread open for SDK PR links and infra ticket updates.

jen: Also add a line in the onboarding checklist: "do not call production side-effect endpoints during SDK init; use warmup probes or a dedicated warmup endpoint."

mira: Thanks all.
